facts.statement: The species was named Lessemsaurus sauropoides by José Fernando Bonaparte in 1999 to honor the science writer Don Lessem.
facts.quote: The type species, L. sauropoides, was formally described by José Fernando Bonaparte in 1999 in honor of Don Lessem, a writer of popular science books.

facts.statement: This extinct sauropodiform dinosaur lived in the Los Colorados Formation of Argentina during the Norian stage of the Upper Triassic.
facts.quote: Lessemsaurus is an extinct genus of sauropodiform dinosaur that lived in the Norian-aged (Upper Triassic) Los Colorados Formation of what is now Argentina.

facts.statement: Fossils of this animal date to the mid-Norian stage, approximately 213 million years ago.
facts.quote: It is part of the La Esquina faunal assemblage, dating to the mid-Norian stage, around 213 million years ago.

facts.statement: Estimates suggest the animal grew to be 10 to 12 meters long and weighed between 7 and 10 metric tons.
facts.quote: It is estimated to have reached 10 - 12 m long and weighed over 7 MT, possibly up to 8 - 10 MT, in maximum body mass.

facts.statement: In 2018, researchers placed the genus in a new family called Lessemsauridae.
facts.quote: In 2018, Apaldetti et al. recovered it as part of a clade they named Lessemsauridae, after Lessemsaurus.

facts.statement: A 2020 study by Oliver W. M. Rauhut and colleagues classified the animal outside the group Sauropoda.
facts.quote: The following cladogram shows the position of Lessemsaurus outside of Sauropoda, according to Oliver W. M. Rauhut and colleagues, 2020

facts.statement: The animal was originally thought to belong to the family Melanorosauridae before being grouped into the new family Lessemsauridae.
facts.quote: Originalmente considerado perteneciente a Melanorosauridae, por lo que se agrupó en una nueva familia, Lessemsauridae junto con Antetonitrus e Ingentia.

facts.statement: The fossil record for this genus spans from 227.3 to 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago)
